## Existing Patterns & Conventions
- Guards that can fail are mutation-tested inside the suite (constitution 3); the mutation must be shown to
  apply before its survival is judged (`tests/smoke.sh:6461`).
- The suite runs on stock macOS bash 3.2 too (`docs/contributing.md:18`, smoke-macos CI), so the guard's
  own code must be bash-3.2 and BSD-tool safe; `awk` is already used by the suite (22 uses in
  `tests/smoke.sh`) and by the hooks (`hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:332`), POSIX features only.
- Same-line `$(`…`)` then `case` is common on today's tree and must not be reported:
  `hooks/lane-guard.sh:31`, `hooks/session-launch.sh:131`, `hooks/session-launch.sh:355`,
  `hooks/status-board.sh:37`, `hooks/status-board.sh:450`, `hooks/ledger-automerge.sh:227`,
  `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:412`. `hooks/status-board.sh:37` also opens `$(` inside a case branch.
- No line in `hooks/*.sh` or `install.sh` ends with an open `$(` today (grep `\$\(\s*$`: no match), so
  the multi-line shape is absent after `8365d75`.
- Heredocs exist in seven hooks (12 openers, e.g. `hooks/session-launch.sh` ×6): their bodies are text,
  so the scanner skips them to their delimiter line.

## Prototype
`prototype-scan.awk` (this directory) is a POSIX-awk scanner of the shape the plan adopts: a stack of
`S` (`$(`), `P` (`(`, `$((` ×2) and `C` (`case`) frames, each `S` saving the quote state it opened in;
single quotes, `$'…'`, double-quoted text, backslash escapes, comments and heredoc bodies skipped; a
`)` while a `C` frame is on top is a case pattern's and does not pop; `esac` pops to its `C`. It prints
`FILE:LINE` for a `case` word read while any `S` frame is on the stack. **Measured (T001, 2026-11-18,
by the orchestrator — headless workers are refused `awk` even with an allow rule, "awk has an option that
can't be checked"):** GNU Awk 5.4.1 over `hooks/*.sh install.sh` at `3af530e` → no output, exit 0, 0.16 s;
over `git show 8365d75^:hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` → `<file>:337`, exactly the old `fg_pushrw` `case` line,
exit 0. A grep of the tree for `case ` after a non-boundary character finds only `ascii_downcase` inside a
jq string (no `case` word). No false positive, so the prototype is cut unchanged. BSD awk was not available
here: the `smoke-macos` CI job is the authority for it (T010).

**Landed guard (T005/T010/T011, 2026-11-18, headless worker).** With `mp_case_in_subst` stubbed to `:`, tier 1
was red on exactly the two expected checks — `FAIL case-in-$( guard must report lines '10 15 19 23 ' of the bad
fixture (got '')` and `FAIL case-in-$( guard must report lost sync on the desync fixture (got '')` (514 passed,
2 failed): SC-001's "fails before". With `MP_CASE_AWK` landed (the prototype transliterated, `'` written `\047`),
tier 1 is `515 passed, 0 failed`; the real-tree check reads `hooks/*.sh install.sh` clean, the bad fixture
reports exactly its four tagged lines (the first is the pre-`8365d75` `fg_pushrw` shape), the good fixture reads
clean, the desync fixture reports lost sync, and all four mutations are caught. SC-002's one-off run of the
landed program on `git show 8365d75^:hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (plan Approach 9) **could not be executed here**:
this worker is refused any `awk` or ad-hoc script invocation outside the suite. The evidence in its place: the
landed program is the measured prototype (which reported `<file>:337` on that file) with only the quote
spelling changed, and the suite's bad-fixture equality proves the landed program reports the same `fg_pushrw`
shape. To close it by hand: source `MP_CASE_AWK` from `tests/smoke.sh` and run `awk "$MP_CASE_AWK"` on that file.
